name: Tata Communications Ltd
title: Tata Communications Ltd - 500483 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 EBITDA up 21.2% to ₹1,422 crore with digital margin at -3.6% from -6.9%, but data revenue grew only ~6% constant currency and capex rose without any numeric capacity guidance.

capex.quote: Cash CapEx trended up this quarter, reflecting investments in our undersea cable assets and DC-to-DC network expansion.

triggers.label: Order book up double digits
triggers.quote: Order book for this quarter has been robust double-digit growth.

triggers.label: Digital margin -6.9% → -3.6%
triggers.quote: The digital portfolio reported EBITDA margin of negative 3.6% versus negative 6.9% in the previous quarter.

triggers.label: Data revenue ~6% constant currency
triggers.quote: Normalizing for the same, data revenues saw a growth of about 6% on a Y-o-Y basis.

guidance.value: Double-digit EBITDA growth this year; digital portfolio EBITDA positive at the soonest
guidance.quote: making sure that we deliver double-digit EBITDA growth this year and turn the digital portfolio to EBITDA positive at the soonest

red_flags.quote: Normalizing for the same, data revenues saw a growth of about 6% on a Y-o-Y basis.

red_flags.label: No numeric capacity or capex guidance
red_flags.quote: we remain focused on scaling capacity in line with customer demand

evasions.quote: I think let's wait one more quarter, you will definitely see.
I haven't put my mind to saying how much of this is AI revenue, I'm not sure whether we are going to go down that path.

summary.headline: Tata Communications Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose 21.2% to ₹1,422 crore, with digital portfolio EBITDA margin improving to -3.6% from -6.9%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 9.6% YoY to ₹6,688 crore and EBITDA grew 21.2% to ₹1,422 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21.3%. Digital portfolio revenue grew 18.6% YoY, and management said digital losses have more than halved versus Q1, nearing EBITDA breakeven. Data revenue grew 12.2% reported but only about 6% after normalising for a stronger dollar. Management said order book grew at a robust double-digit rate, with wins across regions and a growing share from AI-led demand. PAT after minority interest was ₹341 crore, up 86% YoY, and FCF turned positive at ₹212 crore.

segments.name: Digital portfolio
segments.commentary: Revenue up 18.6% YoY, led by interaction, next-gen connectivity and IoT platform. EBITDA margin -3.6% vs -6.9% in Q1, with losses less than half of the previous quarter.

segments.name: Next-gen connectivity
segments.commentary: Growing about 27% YoY per management, with MCC Flex and dynamic DC-to-DC connectivity cited as drivers.

segments.name: Media
segments.commentary: Management said profitability improved and cost initiatives are underway. Revenue remains soft YoY, which management attributed to cyclicality tied to events; LA Olympics support is expected next year.

segments.name: Cloud
segments.commentary: Revenue growth described as muted. Management is shifting toward selling its own sovereign/AI cloud on owned GPUs, with strong India order momentum.

segments.name: Core connectivity (implied)
segments.commentary: An analyst derived an implied core connectivity EBITDA margin of about 44.8%. CFO said it is achievable going forward and that Q2 had no one-offs.

guidance_outlook: Management is committed to double-digit EBITDA growth for FY27 and to making the digital portfolio EBITDA positive as soon as possible.
CFO said the current margin levels, including the about 44.8% implied core connectivity margin, should be achievable in coming quarters, with no one-offs in Q2.
Management plans to share a longer-term growth view and business mix framework at the February Investor Day.
Management expects the order book to convert into revenue in coming quarters, with core connectivity demand expected to show more clearly in revenue after one more quarter.
capex_capacity: Cash capex rose this quarter, driven by undersea cable assets and DC-to-DC network expansion.
Network footprint in India: over 80,000 km of terrestrial fibre, 30,000 km of metro fibre, and connectivity across 118 data centres.
Capacity expansion is tied to anchor-customer demand to keep capital deployment efficient.
GPU utilisation is a focus, as the company has invested in GPUs that it intends to monetise through its own cloud platforms.
demand_pricing: Order book grew at a robust double-digit rate QoQ/YoY, diversified across regions and segments with no large individual wins; some wins came against strong competition.

Recent wins include a multi-million dollar neo-cloud engagement for multi-terabyte connectivity supporting AI data-centre build-out in India, plus Tata Consumer (Sales Saathi) and HDFC ERGO (Voice AI policy servicing).
Pricing model for AI solutions is a fixed SaaS-like platform fee plus usage-based consumables, with revenue allocated back to individual towers.
Management expects 70 PB of traffic by 2036 versus about 2-3 PB currently, citing data-centre-to-data-centre demand.

qa_highlights.question: When will data business show double-digit constant-currency growth given the strong order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was the best order quarter and that much of the book is recurring and network-led; it is watching constant-currency numbers, with H1 EBITDA up about 10% constant currency. It asked investors to wait one more quarter for core connectivity revenue to show.

qa_highlights.question: Is digital margin expansion driven by NR-to-GR mix, and does a higher share of lower-margin CPaaS/collaboration offset this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the improvement reflects mix shift toward platform and recurring revenue with higher sales contribution margin, not just volume. Growth is coming from products with higher profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong core connectivity margin (implied about 44.8%) sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Q2 level and what is achieved should be achievable in coming quarters, and that there were no one-offs affecting Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue model and client count for Commotion/AI offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose client numbers. The model is SaaS-style platform fee plus consumables, spanning network minutes and GPU usage, with revenue flowing back to individual towers.

qa_highlights.question: Is muted cloud growth a deliberate shift toward own Vayu private/sovereign cloud over third-party distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the focus is on selling its own AI and sovereign cloud, using owned GPUs, for better margins, and said India cloud order momentum is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why is media soft YoY, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Media is event-driven and cyclical; some Middle East events were cancelled. Cost initiatives and network synergies are underway, with LA Olympics support expected next year.

risks_watch: Currency: a strengthening dollar cut data revenue growth from 12.2% reported to about 6% normalised.
Core connectivity revenue conversion from the order book has not yet appeared in reported numbers; management asked for one more quarter.
Digital portfolio still EBITDA negative at -3.6%; breakeven timing not quantified.
Canada Revenue Agency in-principle settlement against a ₹1,658 crore contingent liability; terms still being finalised and disclosures pending.
Media revenue remains soft YoY and is event-dependent.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, cash and order book, with specific product examples. Management was guarded on quantification: it declined to disclose AI client counts, gave no digital breakeven date, and deferred medium-term targets to the February Investor Day.
key_quotes: And my single largest focus in the last six months has been profitable growth.
We are very close to EBITDA breakeven for the overall digital portfolio.
Our focus is going to be constant currency growth.
So the shift of the revenue, higher quality revenue, is very important for us.

financial_highlights.change: up 12.2% YoY; about 6% YoY normalised for currency
vs negative FCF in previous quarter

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion

financial_highlights.change: net debt-to-EBITDA 2.17x, steady despite dividend payments

adds.what: Undersea cable assets and DC-to-DC network expansion (cash capex rose; no specific capacity count given)

growth.why: Management reiterated double-digit EBITDA growth for FY27 and digital EBITDA breakeven, backed by a robust double-digit order book growth and capex in undersea cables and DC-to-DC network, though no specific capacity numbers, timelines or revenue growth guidance were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Digital EBITDA margin improved to -3.6% from -6.9% and consolidated EBITDA margin hit 21.3%, with the CFO saying current margin levels including the implied ~44.8% core connectivity margin are achievable with no Q2 one-offs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cash capex rose on undersea cable and DC-to-DC network expansion, but no capacity counts or dates were given and management tied build-out to anchor-customer demand, so new capacity is conditional.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book grew at a robust double-digit rate and Q2 was the best order quarter, with data revenue up 12.2% reported (about 6% constant-currency) and next-gen connectivity up ~27%, though core connectivity conversion is still pending.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was disclosed and capex was described as tied to anchor demand; a formal capex framework is more likely to come at the February Investor Day than in the next quarter.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated rather than raised FY27 EBITDA growth guidance, and it asked investors to wait one more quarter for core connectivity revenue to show.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management is committed to double-digit FY27 EBITDA growth, but H1 EBITDA grew 14.8% and data revenue is only about 6% constant-currency, and a strong dollar or a slow core-connectivity conversion could pressure this.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Commotion/AI offerings, the own sovereign/AI cloud on owned GPUs and next-gen connectivity (MCC Flex, DC-to-DC; ~27% growth) are already in market, though no specific new launch dates were given.

rows.label: Order book conversion to core connectivity revenue
rows.why: Management said the order book will convert into revenue in coming quarters and that core connectivity demand should show more clearly after one more quarter, with Q2 the best order quarter.

rows.label: Digital portfolio EBITDA breakeven
rows.why: Digital EBITDA margin improved to -3.6% from -6.9% (losses less than half the prior quarter), and management is committed to EBITDA-positive digital at the soonest, though no date was given.

rows.label: Canada Revenue Agency settlement vs ₹1,658 crore contingent liability
rows.why: An in-principle settlement has been reached, but terms are still being finalised and disclosures are pending against a ₹1,658 crore contingent liability.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, cash flow (FCF ₹212 crore) and order book momentum, but guarded on quantification, declining to disclose AI client counts and digital breakeven timing and deferring medium-term targets to the February Investor Day; analysts pressed on constant-currency data growt
